summary: This sermon argues that the fall in Genesis was not about choosing evil over good, but about humanity seizing the authority to define wisdom for themselves rather than receiving it from God. Modern technology, especially smartphones, accelerates this same pattern by promising god-like attributes (omniscience, omnipresence, omnipotence) and creating the illusion that we can cultivate Eden-like circumstances apart from relationship with God.
key_points: Human identity as image-bearers and our calling to cultivate Eden has never changed since creation
The tree of knowledge of good and evil represented wisdom itself, which is good, but the issue was the source—trusting God versus seizing autonomy
The fall was choosing good apart from God, defining wisdom for ourselves rather than receiving it from Him
Technology serves as a modern accelerator of the Babel inclination, closing the perceived gap between human and divine wisdom
Jesus models perfect submission to the Father's wisdom, undoing what Adam failed to do, and invites us into that same pattern
big_idea: The core human problem from Genesis to today is choosing to define wisdom and good for ourselves rather than receiving it from God, and technology amplifies this temptation by offering god-like capabilities that promise Eden apart from divine relationship.
title: THE DIGITAL FAST: Sources of Wisdom
